title: A repair you've only watched
topic: Working beyond competence and asking for help
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the labour ward. A midwife asks you to repair a second-degree perineal tear after a normal delivery, as the registrar is in theatre.

You have watched one repair but never done one.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Do the repair, following the steps you observed.
options.detailed: You may remember the steps, but you haven't been trained, and the consequences of a poor repair can be lasting.

options.text: Explain to the midwife that you haven't been trained to do this.
options.brief: Honesty about your limits protects the woman.
options.detailed: A poorly repaired tear can cause long-term problems. Being honest that you haven't been trained is essential.

options.text: Look up a video of the technique, then do the repair.
options.brief: A video doesn't replace supervised training.
options.detailed: Videos can help with learning, but not as a substitute for supervised practice.

options.text: Ask whether a midwife trained in perineal repair is available.
options.brief: Many midwives are trained to repair second-degree tears.
options.detailed: Experienced midwives often repair second-degree tears. One may be available sooner than the registrar.

options.text: Ask the woman whether she minds you doing it for the first time.
options.brief: Her consent doesn't make it safe.
options.detailed: Being open is good, but her agreement doesn't make it appropriate for you to do it untrained and unsupervised.

options.text: Ask the registrar to supervise you doing one when they're free.
options.brief: Supervised practice is how you develop the skill.
options.detailed: A supervised repair, when the registrar is available, lets you learn safely. In the meantime, the woman can be made comfortable.

options.text: Tell the midwife it isn't your job.
options.brief: Unhelpful, and doesn't solve the problem.
options.detailed: You aren't the right person, but you should help find someone who is.

options.text: Ask the midwife to leave the tear until the morning.
options.brief: Delay may increase the risk of complications.
options.detailed: Repairs are usually done promptly, and waiting until morning may not be in the woman's interests.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you recognise the limits of your competence and find a safe way for the woman to receive care.
explanation.keyDetails: You have only observed one repair. The registrar is busy. Trained midwives may be available.
explanation.reasoning: [B] is honest about your limits, [D] finds a trained person, and [F] plans supervised learning. The distractors act beyond competence ([A], [C], [E]), are unhelpful ([G]), or delay care ([H]).
explanation.competing: [E] may seem respectful, but her consent doesn't make an untrained repair safe.
